# matlog

> A local-only BJJ training journal that runs entirely in the browser (a static site on GitHub Pages: no account, no server). The log lives in the browser's IndexedDB, with a copy in localStorage, so an agent can only read or change it by driving a browser with the app open.

App: https://parmsam.github.io/matlog/
Source: https://github.com/parmsam/matlog

## Link actions

Open the app with a `do` query parameter to log something. The parameters are removed from the URL once it has run, and the app shows what it did with an Undo button. Settings never travel in the URL.

- `?do=log&type=open-mat&min=60`: a finished 60-minute open mat that ended now. `type` is class, open-mat, drilling, comp or roll (aliases: lesson, openmat, drill, competition, tournament, round, spar, sparring)
- `?do=start&type=class` / `?do=stop&type=class` / `?do=toggle&type=class`: the timer. One session runs at a time (starting another switches it); a round (`type=roll`) can run inside a session. Stopping a session stops its round
- `&min=90`: length in minutes (1–600). With a length, start and toggle log a finished entry instead
- `&ago=15`: it ended (log) or started (start) 15 minutes ago (0–527040)
- `&gi=gi|nogi`, `&tech=knee cut,armbar from guard` (techniques, comma-separated; unknown names are kept as typed)
- Rounds only: `&partner=Sam&belt=white|blue|purple|brown|black&size=smaller|similar|bigger&sub=armbar,rnc&tapped=triangle&stuck=half guard&outcome=win|loss|draw`
- Moves in a round: `&landed=knee cut,scissor sweep` (you landed them) and `&tried=berimbolo` (you went for it, it didn't land)
- `&note=…` on anything

Examples: `?do=log&type=class&min=90&gi=nogi&tech=knee cut`, `?do=toggle&type=roll`, `?do=log&type=roll&partner=Jo&belt=blue&sub=rnc`.

On iPhone, links open in Safari, which keeps its own data, separate from the Home Screen app.

## Scripting API (in the page)

When you control the page (Playwright `page.evaluate`, DevTools, a browser agent), use `window.matlog`. Calls are synchronous, return plain JSON-safe data, and throw an Error with a readable message on bad input. Names and options match the link actions.

- `matlog.help()`: this reference as text
- `matlog.state()`: `{ name, now, rank: { belt, stripes }, promotions, matHours, sessions, running: [{ type, since, minutes }], workingOn, last7Days: { sessions, minutes, rounds, subsFor, subsAgainst, techniques } }`
- `matlog.log(type, opts?)`, `matlog.start(type, opts?)`, `matlog.stop(type, opts?)`, `matlog.toggle(type, opts?)`: opts are `{ min, minutesAgo, gi, techniques, partner, belt, size, subs, tapped, landed, tried, stuck, outcome, note }` (lists as an array or comma text). Returns `{ result: 'logged' | 'started' | 'stopped' | 'switched', entry }` or `{ result: 'nothing-to-do', reason }`
- `matlog.entries(days = 7)`: sessions, rounds and promotions from the last N days
- `matlog.undo()`: undo the last change made in the app (within 5 minutes)
- `matlog.markdown(days = 7)`: the last N days as Markdown (the same format the Paste dialog reads)
- `matlog.importMarkdown(text)`: log a class note; returns `{ sessions, rounds, ids }`
- `matlog.parseMarkdown(text)`: what importMarkdown would log, without logging
- `matlog.stats()`: subs hit and tapped to, ratio, stuck positions, partners, by partner belt
- `matlog.techniques()`: each technique with sessions drilled, `landed` and `attempts` in rounds, last used, and from → to positions
- `matlog.patterns()`: plain descriptions, each with what it's based on
- `matlog.focus(text?)`: read or set "Working on" (`''` clears). Returns `{ text, since, tracking: { kind, id } | null, sinceThen: { sessions, drilled, attempts, landed, stuck, hit, tapped }, history }`. Only set it when the person asks

## Class note format

```
## No-gi class 2026-10-08 18:00
Length: 90m
Techniques: knee cut, arm triangle
Anything else is the note.

### Rolls
- Sam (purple, bigger, 6m): hit armbar; tapped to triangle; landed knee cut; tried berimbolo; stuck in half guard
```

A heading naming a session (class, open mat, drilling, comp) starts one; a "Rolls" heading lists rounds. Keys: Date, Length, Gi, Techniques, Note, Type. Plain text with no headings is one class.

## Common agent recipes

- Log a 60 minute open mat I just finished
  `matlog.log('open-mat', { min: 60 })`, or open `?do=log&type=open-mat&min=60`.
- I just bowed in to class
  `matlog.start('class')`; later `matlog.stop('class')`.
- Log a round: tapped Sam (purple) with an armbar, got stuck in half guard
  `matlog.log('roll', { partner: 'Sam', belt: 'purple', subs: 'armbar', stuck: 'half guard' })`.
- At open mat I landed a knee cut twice and went for a berimbolo
  One round each: `matlog.log('roll', { landed: 'knee cut', tried: 'berimbolo' })`, `matlog.log('roll', { landed: 'knee cut' })`.
- I'm working on my knee cut
  `matlog.focus('knee cut')`; later `matlog.focus().sinceThen`.
- How many mat hours do I have?
  `matlog.state().matHours`.
- What do I get stuck in, and what do I tap to?
  `matlog.stats()`, or `matlog.patterns()` for sentences.
- Log this class note
  `matlog.importMarkdown(text)`.

## What the app will not do

matlog describes what was logged. It doesn't coach, score, rank you against others or recommend techniques, and agents using it shouldn't present its numbers as advice.
